correctness.rationale: Let B arbitrary BALFI with a∨N(a)=1 and a∧N(a)∧C0(a)=0; for finite subformula-closed set Phi with refuted phi, S observed values, T=S union {1}, r=|T|>=2. The Boolean subalgebra C generated by S,N[S],C0[S] is finite even if BALFI itself is not locally finite; identify its finite atoms Q. Pick first atom separating v(phi) from top, then greedily add an atom from symmetric difference of each unresolved distinct pair in T: number of equivalence classes rises each time from >=2 to r, so choose 1<=|J|<=r-1. Restriction pi:C→P(J) is a Boolean homomorphism, injective on T. At pi(S), unary images N(pi(s))=pi(N(s)) and C0(pi(s))=pi(C0(s)) are well-defined by trace injectivity; off-trace set N(x)=J minus x and C0(x)=J; projected BALFI axioms preserved pointwise. Structural induction gives v′(psi)=pi(v(psi)) for all subformulas, phi still refuted. Since |T|<=t+1, at most t atoms. A trace consisting of top plus r-1 distinct coatoms forces every coordinate, proving optimal r-1 among homomorphic injective trace separators, not arbitrary formula minimal models.
